newsitem.title: UK: UK should lead EMU "outs" -senior UK Conservative.
newsitem.headline: UK should lead EMU "outs" -senior UK Conservative.

text.p: Former Conservative chairman Lord Norman Tebbitt, a prominent "Euro-sceptic", urged the ruling party on Tuesday to unite behind the proposition that Britain should act as leader of those countries that do not join Europe's planned single currency.

In a speech on the fringe of the Conservatives' annual conference, Tebbitt warned that economic and monetary union (EMU) would do great economic damage in Europe and, by inducing monetary instability, probably in the wider world, too.
He said he agreed with Prime Minister John Major that Britain should be in the negotiations for EMU, due to be launched in 1999, until the very end.
"But I do not believe that is incompatible with saying that Britain will not participate in the first wave.
"After all, it is Britain's role to lead. There will not be a single currency in 1999. There may be an enlarged deutschemark zone in which some countries become economic colonies of Germany.

"But there will be 'outs' as well as 'ins'. Surely Britain has a role in leading the 'outs' to ensure that there is a fair relationship between 'outs' and "ins'. On that at least the party -- other than a handful of federalists -- should be able to unite," Tebbitt said.
